newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BAGACH SAYS HE TOOK BANNED DRUG IN ERROR.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAGACH SAYS HE TOOK BANNED DRUG IN ERROR.

text.p: Aleksandr Bagach, stripped of his world shot put gold medal and $60,000 prize money on Thursday, said he had taken the banned stimulant ephedrine in error.
"Basically I used this supplement which is made of natural substances and does not mention that it has ephedrine in it," the 30-year-old Ukrainian told Reuters Television.
"I obtained the product in Kiev from the official representative of the manufacturing company who assured me there was nothing forbidden in the ingredients.
"I first used it at the world championships in Paris and when I tested I was negative."
The International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) said earlier on Thursday that the Olympic bronze medallist had tested positive for ephedrine and would lose his title and prize money.

French 400 metres hurdler Pascal Maran and women's triple jumper Oxana Zelinskaya of Kazakhstan, neither of whom made the finals, also tested positive for ephedrine and their results were also cancelled.
Bagach, who has already served a doping suspension, was the first person to win a gold medal here and the first person to test positive for drugs.
Valery Alexandrov, vice-president of the Ukrainian federation, criticised athletics officials in the Ukraine for not informing the team that the supplement Bagach had used had contained banned drugs.
"The mistake of this athlete is that he used this substance without knowing that this pseudo-ephedrine was in it," Alexandrov said.
"No competent authorities informed us of this and there are no adequate laboratories in Ukraine to do a check on this product."

Bagach is lucky in one respect. As the IAAF relaxed their doping rules just before the championships, all three will receive a public warning but will be free to continue competing in lucrative grand prix meetings after the championships.

"Following the recent decision by the IAAF congress, these athletes will be issued a public warning and disqualified from the competition," the IAAF said in a statement. "The results they achieved at these world championships have been cancelled."

American John Godina, who received a wild card entry as defending champion, will now take the shot gold medal, German Oliver-Sven Buder the silver and another American, C.J. Hunter, fiancee of new world 100 metres champion Marion Jones, has been awarded the bronze.
Bagach was banned for two years in 1989 after he was found to have excessive levels of the male hormone testosterone in his body when he was competing for the former Soviet Union.
"I can't say how I feel," Bagach said. "I haven't got over it yet, I haven't recovered yet."
French officials said Maran had already left Athens and but could still face a tougher penalty from his national authority.
"The French federation has not changed its rules," French team doctor Herve de Labareyre said. "(But) He will probably face a suspended sentence from the French federation."
